mainTopic: Whether a fetus can be held back from its mother (שיירו משוייר), רבי יוחנן's view and its reason, and changing one's mind when giving an animal a holy name.
overview: The גמרא uses the rule that a freed slave's document and his power to receive it arrive together. From this it argues that a mother can acquire freedom for her fetus only if the fetus is part of her body. That leads to the conclusion that שיירו אינו משוייר, and רבי יוחנן is refuted. The גמרא then tries to show that שיירו משוייר is an argument between תנאים. It first brings the case of a freed pregnant שפחה, and then two ברייתות about a live fetus found inside a slaughtered חטאת. Each time it answers that everyone may agree, and the dispute is about something else: a special פסוק about slaves, when ולדי קדשים become holy, or which came first, the pregnancy or the consecration. רבא suggests רבי יוחנן's real reason might be אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש. רב המנונא rejects this, because רבי יוחנן never gave that answer to his student רבי אלעזר. רב פפא explains that the משנה's ruling about changing one's mind is needed for a change within תוך כדי דיבור. A new משנה then has רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about an animal given two names: the תמורה of an עולה and of a שלמים.

steps.title: Freeing half a slave: document and power arrive together
steps.stepSummary: A master who frees half his slave makes that half free, because the document and the slave's ability to receive it arrive at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone frees half of his slave, that half goes free. His freedom document and his ability to receive it come at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule about how a slave can receive his own freedom document. This rule is the base for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a slave cannot acquire anything for himself, because whatever he takes belongs to his master. Here the slave still gets his freedom, because the גט שחרור gives him the power to acquire at the very moment he receives it. The next step uses this idea to show that a mother can only receive freedom for her fetus if the fetus is part of her body.

keyTerms.meaning: one who frees a slave
freedom
his freedom document and his ability to receive it come together at the same moment

phrases.english: One who frees half of his slave
he goes out to freedom (that half),
his document and his hand come at the same time.
phrases.notes: His 'hand' means his power to take something for himself. A slave usually doesn't have that power.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about freeing a pregnant שפחה and her fetus.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave can receive his own freedom document because the document and his power to acquire arrive at the same time.

steps.title: If the fetus is separate, how can the mother receive its freedom?
steps.stepSummary: If a fetus is not part of its mother (שיירו משוייר), the mother could not receive freedom for it, since a slave cannot receive a freedom document for a fellow slave from their shared master.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that holding something back works, and a fetus is not part of its mother, why does she acquire freedom for it? We learned in a ברייתא that a slave can receive another slave's freedom document from that slave's master if he is not his own master, but not from his own master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that a fetus is a separate being. It uses a ברייתא about one slave receiving a freedom document for another slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fetus were separate from the mother, she would be receiving a freedom document for a 'fellow slave' from their shared master. The ברייתא says that does not work, because a slave's hand is his master's hand. Yet earlier we saw that she does acquire for the fetus. That only makes sense if the fetus is part of her body, so her own גיטו וידו באין כאחת covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: if he held it back, it stays held back (a reservation works)
a fetus is like its mother's thigh, meaning part of her body
she acquired on its behalf
a slave's freedom document

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying a slave can never act for another slave. It only blocks receiving the document from their own shared master, because anything he receives from that master stays in the master's hands.

phrases.english: And if you say: if he held it back, it is held back,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's view: when someone makes an animal holy, he can keep its fetus out of the הקדש.

phrases.english: a fetus is not the thigh of its mother,
why does she acquire for it?
But isn't it taught:
It appears that a slave can acquire

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 1 together with a ברייתא to attack שיירו משוייר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that שיירו משוייר, meaning the fetus is a separate being
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate fetus would be a 'fellow slave' of the same master. A slave cannot receive a freedom document for a fellow slave from their shared master, yet the mother does acquire for the fetus.

steps.title: Conclusion: holding back does not work, so רבי יוחנן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שיירו אינו משוייר, and that רבי יוחנן is truly refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that if he held it back, it is not held back, and the refutation of רבי יוחנן is a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion: a fetus is part of its mother, so trying to hold it back does not work. רבי יוחנן's opinion is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only way the mother can acquire freedom for the fetus is if the fetus counts as part of her. Then you cannot hold a fetus back while including the mother, so רבי יוחנן's position does not stand. The word תיובתא appears twice to stress that this is a final refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this, a conclusion
holding it back does not work
a decisive refutation

steps.whatToRemember: The fetus is treated as part of its mother (עובר ירך אמו). So שיירו אינו משוייר, and רבי יוחנן is refuted.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
if he held it back, it is not held back,
and the refutation of Rabbi Yochanan is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the challenge in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שיירו אינו משוייר, and רבי יוחנן is refuted.

steps.title: Is this question a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שיירו משוייר may be a dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים, about freeing a שפחה while keeping her child a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that 'if he held it back, it is held back' is a dispute of תנאים? A ברייתא teaches: if a master tells his שפחה, 'You are free and your child is a slave,' her child is like her. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי. The חכמים say his words stand, because it says, 'The woman and her children shall be her master's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Maybe the issue of holding back a fetus is really argued about by תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the child goes free with its mother, which fits the view that a fetus is part of her and cannot be held back. The חכמים say the master's words stand and the child stays a slave, which fits שיירו משוייר. If so, רבי יוחנן would have support from the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say, a suggestion the גמרא tests
it is a dispute between תנאים
a maidservant (a Canaanite slave woman)
a free woman
his words stand, meaning they take effect

phrases.english: Shall we say that 'if he held it back, it is held back'
is a dispute of tannaim?
As it is taught: One who says to his maidservant,
"You are hereby a free woman, and your child a slave"
her child is like her,
the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
And the Sages say: his words stand,
because it is said:

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אִם שִׁיְּירוֹ מְשׁוּיָּיר תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After refuting רבי יוחנן, the גמרא asks whether his view has support among the תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is שיירו משוייר the subject of the dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים?

steps.title: How does the פסוק help the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק 'the woman and her children shall be her master's' supports the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק: what lesson does it give the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the ברייתא. The פסוק the חכמים quote seems to prove the opposite of what they say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the children to the mother: they go wherever she goes. That sounds like the child is free when the mother is free, which is רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. So it is hard to see how the חכמים can use it to prove the child stays a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק
what is the lesson, meaning how is it learned from here

phrases.english: The verse, what is its lesson for the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the פסוק that step 4 quotes for the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of the פסוק as the source for the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק links the children to their mother, which seems to support רבי יוסי הגלילי rather than the חכמים.

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק is really רבי יוסי הגלילי's source
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the פסוק in the ברייתא is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי: as long as the woman belongs to her master, so does her child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the פסוק is said for רבי יוסי הגלילי, who teaches that her child is like her, as it says, 'The woman and her children shall be her master's.' When the woman belongs to her master, her child belongs to her master.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reading the ברייתא differently. The פסוק is the proof for רבי יוסי הגלילי, not for the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the פסוק teaches that the child follows the mother's status. It belongs to the master only while she does, so when she goes free, it goes free too. The next steps ask whether רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling also shows that he holds a fetus is part of its mother.

keyTerms.meaning: her child has the same status as her
at the time that, meaning as long as

phrases.english: Rava said:
the verse is stated for Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
as it teaches: her child is like her,
as it is said: "The woman and her children shall be her master's"
when the woman belongs to her master,
her child belongs to her master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא: the פסוק belongs to the other opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to quote the פסוק as proof for the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is the proof for רבי יוסי הגלילי: the child follows the mother, belonging to the master only while she does.

steps.title: Suggesting that רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים argue about שיירו משוייר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the dispute about freeing a שפחה is really about whether שיירו משוייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it true that this is exactly what they argue about? רבי יוסי holds that if the owner held back the fetus, it is not held back, and the חכמים hold that it is held back.
steps.whatsHappening: After clearing up the פסוק, the גמרא returns to its suggestion: the argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים is about שיירו משוייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this suggestion, רבי יוסי הגלילי says the child goes free with the mother because a fetus cannot be held back from its mother. The חכמים say the owner can free the mother and keep the child, so שיירו משוייר. If so, the question becomes an argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it true that...? (a way of offering a suggestion)
they argue
if he held it back, it is held back (the fetus can be kept apart from the mother)

phrases.english: What, is it not that they argue about this:
that Rabbi Yosei holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי הגלילי from the ברייתא about freeing the שפחה.

phrases.english: if he held it back, it is not held back,
and the Rabbis hold: it is held back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבא has explained the פסוק, the גמרא spells out what it thinks the argument in step 4 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים really about שיירו משוייר?

steps.title: Everyone may agree; רבי יוסי הגלילי relies on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן could answer that everyone holds שיירו משוייר, and רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling comes only from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: Everyone agrees that if he held it back, it is held back. Here the reason is that the פסוק says: 'The woman and her children shall be her master's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion and says this case does not prove an argument about שיירו משוייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees that a fetus can normally be held back. The child goes free with the mother only because of a special rule from the פסוק: a slave woman's child follows her status. So the argument is about how to read the פסוק, not about the general idea.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees
this is the reason

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling here is a special rule for slaves taken from a פסוק. It does not show that he holds a fetus can never be held back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you:
Everyone agrees that if he held it back, it is held back,
and here this is the reason:
because the verse says:
"The woman and her children shall be her master's."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שִׁיְּירוֹ מְשׁוּיָּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 7's claim that the argument is about שיירו משוייר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling may come from a special פסוק about slaves, not from the general question of שיירו משוייר.

steps.title: A different pair of תנאים: the first ברייתא on a fetus found in a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question is surely an argument between other תנאים. The first ברייתא treats a live fetus found in a slaughtered חטאת as a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we must certainly say it is like these תנאים, as it was taught: If someone slaughters a חטאת and finds a live four-month-old fetus inside it, one ברייתא teaches: It is eaten only by male כהנים, only for one day, and only inside the curtains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the first pair of תנאים and brings a new dispute between two ברייתות. Here it quotes the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a live fetus found inside a slaughtered חטאת. The first ברייתא gives the fetus all the strict rules of a חטאת: only male כהנים may eat it, only for one day, and only in the holy area. So it treats the fetus as having the same status as its mother.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, certainly
תנאים, sages of the משנה era
a sin offering
male כהנים
inside the curtains, the holy courtyard area

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא וַדַּאי לֵימָא כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, certainly let us say it is like these tanna'im,
as it is taught: One who slaughters a sin offering
and found in it a live four-month-old fetus,

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: אֵין נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לְזִכְרֵי כְהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: one ברייתא teaches: It is eaten only by males of the priesthood,
and it is eaten only for one day,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים.
phrases.english: and it is eaten only inside the curtains.
phrases.notes: The curtains surrounded the courtyard of the משכן, so this means inside the holy courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא וַדַּאי לֵימָא כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first pair of תנאים, the גמרא offers a new source for the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That the status of a fetus, compared with its mother, is an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first of two ברייתות about a fetus found in a slaughtered חטאת.

steps.title: The second ברייתא: the fetus may be eaten by anyone
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא rules that the fetus may be eaten by any person, in any place, at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: It may be eaten by any person, in any place, and forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא, which disagrees with the first. Now both sides of the dispute are on the table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא removes every limit of a חטאת: who may eat it, where, and for how long. It treats the fetus as ordinary meat, not holy, so its status is separate from its mother's.

keyTerms.meaning: the other one (here, the other ברייתא)
for any person
forever, with no time limit

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות disagree. The first treats a fetus found in a חטאת as a חטאת, like its mother. The second treats it as ordinary food that anyone may eat.

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches: It is eaten by any person,
and it is eaten in any place,
and it is eaten forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing ברייתא, completing the dispute between תנאים begun in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the status of a fetus, compared with its mother, is an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second ברייתא, which treats the fetus as ordinary meat.

steps.title: The two ברייתות seem to argue about holding back the fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא holds שיירו אינו משוייר, while the second ברייתא holds שיירו משוייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this an argument between תנאים? The first תנא holds that if he holds back the fetus, it is not held back. The other Sage holds that if he holds it back, it is held back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in steps 9 and 10. It reads the two ברייתות as a real argument about שיירו משוייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא calls the fetus a חטאת, which suggests the fetus is just part of its mother. The second ברייתא lets anyone eat the fetus, which suggests the fetus is its own separate thing. If that reading is right, רבי יוחנן's rule is only one side of an argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: If he held it back, it stays held back. The fetus can be left out when the mother is consecrated.
An argument between תנאים, the Sages of the משנה period
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: What, is it not a dispute of tanna'im,
that the first tanna holds:
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא from step 9, which treats the live fetus as a חטאת.

phrases.english: "he reserved it" — it is not reserved,
and the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא from step 10, which lets anyone eat the fetus.

phrases.english: "he reserved it" — it is reserved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the two ברייתות quoted in steps 9 and 10.
steps.raayaObject: That שיירו משוייר is an argument between תנאים, so רבי יוחנן holds like only one side
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two ברייתות about a live fetus found inside a slaughtered חטאת

steps.title: Everyone agrees the fetus can be held back; the argument is about when offspring become holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that everyone holds שיירו משוייר. The ברייתות argue about whether ולדי קדשים become holy at birth or already in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could tell you: everyone agrees that if he holds it back, it is held back. These תנאים argue about something else. One Sage holds that the offspring of קדשים become holy when they come into being, at birth. The other Sage holds that they become holy while still in their mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from step 11. It moves the argument onto a different question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is an animal that was consecrated first and became pregnant later, so nobody held anything back. If offspring become holy only at birth, a fetus that was never born is never holy, and anyone may eat it. If offspring become holy in the womb, the fetus is already a חטאת. Either way, the argument has nothing to do with שיירו.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
The offspring of animals that were consecrated as קרבנות
When they come into being, meaning when they are born
In their mother's womb

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two questions. שיירו is about whether the owner can choose to leave the fetus out. The new argument is about when an unborn offspring becomes holy at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan could say to you:
Everyone holds that if he reserved it, it is reserved,
and these tanna'im disagree about this:
one Sage holds:
the offspring of sacrificial animals become holy when they come into being,
phrases.notes: "Come into being" means being born. So a fetus that was never born never became holy.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds:

phrases.aramaic: וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים.
phrases.english: the offspring of sacrificial animals become holy in their mother's womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִם שִׁיְּירוֹ מְשׁוּיָּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back step 11's reading of the two ברייתות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the ברייתות argue about שיירו. The ברייתות still argue, but about something else.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות can be explained as arguing over when ולדי קדשים become holy, not over holding back the fetus.

steps.title: Another answer: the two ברייתות describe different cases
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: there is no argument at all. One ברייתא is about an animal consecrated before it became pregnant. The other is about an animal consecrated after it became pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: there is no difficulty. Here, he consecrated the animal and only later it became pregnant. There, it became pregnant first and only later he consecrated it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer step 11. This time, the two ברייתות do not disagree at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that שיירו משוייר, and everyone agrees that offspring become holy at birth. If the animal became pregnant only after it was consecrated, the fetus was never consecrated and never born, so anyone may eat it (the second ברייתא). If the animal was already pregnant when it was consecrated and nothing was held back, the fetus was consecrated together with its mother as a חטאת (the first ברייתא).

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say. This opens a second, alternative answer.
It is not difficult. The two sources do not really contradict each other.
He consecrated it, the mother animal
It became pregnant

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות do not prove that שיירו משוייר is an argument between תנאים. In רבי יוחנן's answer, everyone agrees that holding back works. The ברייתות either argue about when offspring become holy, or describe two different cases depending on what came first: the consecration or the pregnancy.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: it is not difficult,
here, where he consecrated it
phrases.notes: "Here" is the second ברייתא, the one that lets anyone eat the fetus.

phrases.english: and only afterward it became pregnant,
there, where it became pregnant
phrases.notes: "There" is the first ברייתא, where the fetus is a חטאת.

phrases.english: and only afterward he consecrated it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 11, different from the answer in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects any argument between the ברייתות at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 11 assumed both ברייתות discuss the same case. They actually differ in whether the pregnancy came before or after the consecration.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fetus present at the time of consecration becomes holy with its mother. Fetus conceived after the consecration and never born stays non-holy.

steps.title: רבא questions the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how we know רבי יוחנן's reason is שיירו משוייר. Maybe his reason is that a person can get atonement with שבח הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: How do we know that רבי יוחנן's reason is that if a person holds back the fetus, it stays held back? Maybe his real reason is that a person can gain atonement through the growth of a holy animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the assumption that רבי יוחנן's ruling is built on שיירו משוייר. He offers a different reason that could explain the same ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion so far took for granted that רבי יוחנן holds שיירו משוייר. רבא says the ruling could also be explained by a different rule: אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש. On that view, the fetus is just extra 'growth' of the holy animal, and a person can bring it for his atonement. If רבא is right, we cannot prove that רבי יוחנן holds שיירו משוייר.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; a strong challenge against a statement
Perhaps; maybe it is really like this
If he held it back, it stays held back (the fetus is not included in the mother's holiness)
A person can gain atonement through the growth or increase of a holy animal

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about what רבי יוחנן ruled. He only questions WHY רבי יוחנן ruled that way.

phrases.english: Rava objects to this:
From where do we know that Rabbi Yochanan's reason
is that if he held it back, it stays held back?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the fetus inside the mother when he made the mother holy.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is Rabbi Yochanan's reason:
that a person can gain atonement through the growth of holy property.
phrases.notes: The newborn is treated like extra growth of the holy mother animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: מִמַּאי דְּטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared assumption behind the earlier discussion that רבי יוחנן holds שיירו משוייר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוחנן's ruling is based on שיירו משוייר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ruling can be explained by another principle, אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש, so it does not prove שיירו משוייר.

steps.title: רב המנונא: רבי יוחנן never gave that answer to his student
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers רבא: רבי אלעזר questioned רבי יוחנן assuming שיירו משוייר, and רבי יוחנן never answered with the reason of שבח הקדש. So that cannot be his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to him: רבי אלעזר was רבי יוחנן's student and sat in front of him, and רבי יוחנן did not give him this answer. And you say that רבי יוחנן's reason is that a person can gain atonement through the growth of holy property?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא defends the original assumption. He points out that רבי יוחנן himself never used רבא's explanation, even when it would have helped him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר questioned רבי יוחנן on the assumption that his reason was שיירו משוייר. If רבי יוחנן's real reason had been שבח הקדש, he could have simply said so and the question would have gone away. Since he did not, we can tell that his reason really is שיירו משוייר.

keyTerms.meaning: His student
Answered him back; replied to him
An answer or explanation given to resolve a question

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion stands: רבי יוחנן's ruling is based on שיירו משוייר, not on שבח הקדש. We know this because he did not use the שבח הקדש answer when his own student questioned him.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said to him:
Rabbi Elazar was the student of Rabbi Yochanan,
and he sat before Rabbi Yochanan,
and he did not reply to him with this answer,
and you say that Rabbi Yochanan's reason
is because a person can gain atonement through the growth of holy property?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection and restores the assumption that רבי יוחנן holds שיירו משוייר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from silence: the master did not use the alternative answer when it would have helped him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling might come from אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's reason is שיירו משוייר, since he did not answer his student with the שבח הקדש reason.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say a change of mind after the declaration does not help?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if he changed his mind only after saying 'this is a שלמים', the offspring is a שלמים. It asks: isn't that obvious? A person cannot change his mind whenever he wants!
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If he changed his mind after saying 'This animal is a peace offering,' and so on. The גמרא asks: That is obvious, their offspring are peace offerings! Can a person just change his mind whenever he wants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the משנה and quotes it. Then it challenges the משנה, saying its ruling is so obvious that it did not need to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he said 'this animal is a שלמים', the animal and its fetus already became holy as a שלמים. Saying afterwards 'its offspring is an עולה' should not be able to undo that. So the גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to teach something this obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: He changed his mind; he reconsidered
It is obvious! (a challenge: why teach this?)
Their offspring
Whenever he wants

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִשֶּׁאָמַר ״הֲרֵי זוֹ שְׁלָמִים״ נִמְלַךְ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: If he changed his mind after he said 'This is a peace offering,' etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: afterwards he said 'its offspring is an עולה', and the offspring stays a שלמים.

phrases.english: It is obvious that their offspring are peace offerings,
can he change his mind whenever he wants?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מִשֶּׁאָמַר הֲרֵי זוֹ שְׁלָמִים נִמְלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן discussion and returns to explain a new clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the offspring stays a שלמים when he changed his mind after declaring the mother a שלמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A declaration that already took effect cannot be undone by a later change of mind, so the ruling seems too obvious to need teaching.

steps.title: רב פפא: The case is a change of mind within תוך כדי דיבור
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה is talking about someone who changed his mind within תוך כדי דיבור. We might have thought this counts as one continuous statement, so the משנה teaches that it does not help here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This was needed only when he said it within the time it takes to say a short phrase. You might have thought that within that short time it counts as one continuous statement, and that he was just still thinking it through. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the 'obvious' question by narrowing the case. The משנה is about a person who changed his mind almost right away, within תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he changed his mind very quickly, we might think the two statements join into one, so the offspring would become an עולה. We might say he was not really changing his mind, only still thinking it over. The משנה teaches that even so, the offspring stays a שלמים, so the ruling is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for this case (narrowing the case to show the ruling is not obvious)
Within the time it takes to say a short greeting; a very short pause
You might have said; you might have thought
He was just still thinking it over
It teaches us (that this mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'obvious' ruling of the משנה is needed for a change of mind within תוך כדי דיבור. Even then, the offspring stays a שלמים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't take this as throwing out תוך כדי דיבור everywhere. רב פפא only says the משנה teaches that here, the quick change of mind does not help.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It was needed only
where he said it within the time of speaking a short phrase,
phrases.notes: He said 'its offspring is an עולה' right after calling the mother a שלמים.

phrases.english: you might have said
that within the time of speaking a short phrase counts as continuous speech,
and this man was just still thinking it over —
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא שֶׁאָמַר בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִּיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the משנה to a change of mind within תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A change of mind within תוך כדי דיבור joins the first statement, so the offspring would be an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even within תוך כדי דיבור, the offspring stays a שלמים, as the משנה teaches.

steps.title: The new משנה: two designations, and רבי מאיר says the first one wins
steps.stepSummary: A person calls one animal 'the תמורה of an עולה, the תמורה of a שלמים.' רבי מאיר rules that it is the תמורה of the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'This animal is the substitute of a burnt offering, the substitute of a peace offering,' it is the substitute of the burnt offering. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It presents a case where a person gives one animal two different names, and רבי מאיר rules that only the first name counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person has an עולה and a שלמים, and he names a third, ordinary animal as the תמורה of both. רבי מאיר holds that once the first words 'תמורת עולה' are said, they take hold, and the second words cannot change that. So the animal becomes the תמורה of the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an ordinary animal that someone tries to swap for a קרבן. It becomes holy too
A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
A peace offering, which is mostly eaten by the owners

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'הרי זו תמורת עולה' appear twice. The first time is the person speaking. The second time is רבי מאיר's ruling about what the animal becomes.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"This is hereby the substitute of a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: He has an עולה and a שלמים in front of him, and he is talking about a third, ordinary animal.

phrases.english: the substitute of a peace offering"
it is the substitute of the burnt offering;
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֲרֵי זוֹ תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה תְּמוּרַת שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of changing one's mind in steps 16–17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, when one animal is given two designations one after the other, the first designation takes effect: it is the תמורה of the עולה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: it depends on what he meant from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that if he planned both names from the beginning, both of his words take effect. If he changed his mind after saying 'עולה', it stays an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: If that is what he meant from the start, then both of his words stand, since it is impossible to say two names at once. But if after he said 'substitute of a burnt offering' he changed his mind and said 'substitute of a peace offering', it is the substitute of the burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר. He splits the case into two: either the person planned both names from the start, or he changed his mind partway through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason is that nobody can say two names in one breath, so a person who wants both must say them one after the other. If that was his plan all along, both names take effect. But if the second name was a new thought, the first name has already taken hold, and the animal stays the תמורה of the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended it from the start
Two names (designations) at the same moment
His words stand: what he said takes effect
He changed his mind (had a second thought)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the first words win. רבי יוסי: look at what he planned. If he meant both from the start, both take effect. If the second name was only a change of mind, the first one wins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the idea of the earlier משנה (steps 16–17): once a designation has taken hold, a later change of mind cannot undo it. רבי יוסי adds that a planned two-part statement is treated as one statement.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי said:
If that is what he intended at the start,
phrases.notes: He means: he planned from the beginning to name it for both the עולה and the שלמים.

phrases.english: since it is impossible
to call out two names at once,
his words stand;
but if, after he said "substitute of a burnt offering,"
he changed his mind and said "substitute of a peace offering,"
it is the substitute of the burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִם לְכֵן נִתְכַּוֵּין תְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's ruling in step 18 by making the outcome depend on the person's original intent
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, if both names were intended from the start, both take effect, because two names cannot be said at once. If the second name came only from a change of mind, the animal is the תמורה of the עולה.
